segments.he: ״הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר מִן הַגְּרוֹגְרוֹת וּמִן הַדְּבֵילָה״, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: נָזִיר. וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: אֵינוֹ נָזִיר. אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: אַף כְּשֶׁאָמְרוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי, לֹא אָמְרוּ אֶלָּא בְּאוֹמֵר ״הֲרֵי הֵן עָלַי קׇרְבָּן״.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» If one says: «I am hereby a nazirite» and therefore will refrain «from dried figs and from cakes of dried figs, Beit Shammai say:» His statement renders him a full-fledged «nazirite,» and his addition: From dried figs, is insignificant, as this fruit is not included in the prohibitions of a nazirite, which include only products of the grapevine. «And Beit Hillel say: He is not a nazirite,» since he did not accept naziriteship upon himself. «Rabbi Yehuda said: Even when Beit Shammai said» that this vow takes effect, «they said» that «only in» a case «where» one «said» that he meant: «They are hereby» forbidden «to me» as «an offering.» In that case it is as though he took a vow rendering the figs forbidden to him. However, Beit Shammai concede that although the vow takes effect, it is not a vow of naziriteship.
